sections.title: Employment
descriptions: Officer Bronson T. Kitchen began working for the American Fork Police Department on August 5, 2024. Before joining AFPD, he held public-sector positions with Salt Lake County, the State of Utah, and the Utah Transit Authority.

Public compensation records show Bronson T. Kitchen working in several public-sector positions before joining the American Fork Police Department. In 2018, the Utah Transit Authority reported him under the titles Bus Operator Trainee and Extra Board Operator, a relief-driver position used to cover routes as needed. State of Utah records list him as a POST-certified correctional officer in 2020 and 2021. Salt Lake County subsequently listed him as a Deputy II in 2023 and 2024. By 2025, American Fork City employed him as a Police Officer I.
He also is the school resource officer for American Fork Jr. High School.

transcript of Chief Cameron Paul’s September 16, 2026 interview with Daniel Sroka
records the following comments. Quotations below are from the final edited transcript.

contents.text_value: Discussing Kitchen’s continued school assignment, Chief Paul described discipline and said the assignment depended on Kitchen doing his job well:

segments.text: “With Bronson, we've told him, “You messed up. You're disciplined. Here are the things. Just so you know, if this happens again, there's going to be some serious issues.””

“He doesn't have an employment right to just be up at the junior high. He's got to be doing his job, and doing it well. When that changes—which I don't think it will, but if it does—we'll make a change.”
Chief Paul also said the principal supported retaining Kitchen, while acknowledging that he was relying on the principal’s account of conditions at the school.
